content.value_statement: Subscription billing requires coordinated lifecycle, payment, invoice, tax, and recovery rules. This skill provides practical patterns for designing and validating those workflows.
actual_capabilities: Maps trial, active, past-due, paused, resumed, and canceled subscription states.
Outlines recurring billing cycles, renewals, cancellations, and payment processing.
Provides invoice generation patterns with line items, tax, totals, and status transitions.
Calculates plan, seat, and usage-based charges with proration examples.
Designs retry schedules, customer notifications, grace periods, and cancellation rules.
Reviews regional sales tax, VAT, and GST requirements at a planning level.
limitations: The examples are illustrative and require integration with your billing provider and data model.
Tax rates and rules are incomplete and require current professional validation.
The skill does not execute payments or deploy a billing system by itself.
Production use requires sandbox testing, security review, reconciliation, and compliance checks.

use_cases.title: Launch SaaS Subscriptions
use_cases.description: Define plans, lifecycle states, invoices, renewals, and payment behavior for a new subscription product.

use_cases.title: Improve Payment Recovery
use_cases.description: Create balanced retry schedules, notices, grace periods, and account restrictions for failed payments.

use_cases.title: Review Billing Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess proration, usage metering, taxes, audit trails, and reconciliation before production rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Basic Billing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monthly subscription plan for [product]. Include price, trial length, renewal timing, cancellation behavior, and invoice timing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a simple subscription product.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Subscription Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Map lifecycle states for [product]. Define allowed transitions, triggers, customer notifications, payment effects, and recovery actions for each state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when formalizing subscription behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Dunning and Proration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create dunning and proration rules for [plans]. Include retry timing, grace periods, upgrades, downgrades, seat changes, credits, and test cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when billing changes and failed payments need coordinated rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Billing Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this billing design: [design]. Identify lifecycle gaps, duplicate-charge risks, tax assumptions, reconciliation needs, failure modes, and sandbox validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before production rollout or a major billing migration.

output_examples.input: Design failed-payment recovery for a monthly team plan.
output: Day 0: Mark the invoice past due and notify the billing contact.
Day 3: Retry payment and provide a secure payment-update link.
Day 7: Retry again and warn about upcoming account restrictions.
Day 14: Make the final attempt, then apply the documented cancellation policy.

output_examples.input: Explain an upgrade from a monthly basic plan to a pro plan halfway through the cycle.
output_examples.output: Credit the unused basic-plan period, charge the remaining pro-plan period, and show both adjustments on the invoice. Test rounding and timezone boundaries.

output: Define each billable metric and its source of truth.
Prevent duplicate usage events with stable identifiers.
Close metering periods before invoice finalization.
Reconcile aggregated usage against source events before charging customers.

best_practices: Use idempotency controls and durable audit records for every charge, invoice, retry, and subscription transition.
Validate payment flows with sandbox data and reconcile invoices against ledger outputs before release.
Confirm tax, privacy, and notification obligations for every supported region.
anti_patterns: Do not test billing logic by charging real customers.
Do not hardcode tax rates, billing dates, or retry rules without controlled configuration and review.
Do not finalize invoices before validating usage, proration, discounts, tax, and payment state.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to a payment provider?
faq.answer: No. It provides design patterns and examples that you must adapt to your selected provider.

faq.question: Can it calculate proration?
faq.answer: It provides formulas and examples for plan and seat changes. You must validate rounding, credits, dates, and provider behavior.

faq.question: Does it support usage-based billing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers usage tracking and tiered, per-unit, and volume pricing at an implementation-pattern level.

faq.question: Can I rely on the included tax rates?
faq.answer: No. The rates are examples and are not complete or current tax advice.

faq.question: How should failed payments be handled?
faq.answer: Define retry timing, notices, grace periods, restrictions, recovery actions, and cancellation rules that match your customer policy.

faq.question: What validation is required before production?
faq.answer: Test lifecycle transitions, duplicate prevention, rounding, timezones, retries, taxes, invoice delivery, and ledger reconciliation in a sandbox.
